title: Velocity-latency tiered bench notes
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working notes from a set of microbench runs comparing a three-tier model serving strategy under three velocity profiles (micro-session, burst, sustained). Goal: capture sketch-level latency vs $/1k tradeoffs and flag promising knobs for Optimize and Console teams (prefetch, handshake window, elastic tiering).

High-level summary (no slides):
- Tiering (small->medium->large) gives strong $/1k improvements for micro-session use cases but amplifies tail latency under high-cardinality bursts if KV hit rate falls.
- Prefetch/handshake sizing (0.2s-0.6s window) materially reduces p90 for medium tier without large cost increase because it increases cache reuse.
- Quantization profile (q4_0 vs q8_0) moves cost curve left but can add 10-25% p90 overhead for long-context decoding on large models; consider hybrid: q4 for short-turn, q8 for long-turn.

Methodology (short):
- Hardware: A100x2 (hosted) for medium/large, T4 equivalence emulated for small tier to match edge ev combos.
- Models: small=7B q4_0, medium=13B q4_0, large=70B q8_0. (We intentionally used mixed quant to reflect current catalog).
- Workloads: micro-session (single-turn, <40 tokens), burst (10k qps sustained for 60s with Poisson arrivals), sustained (steady 200 qps for 30m).
- Concurrency knobs: default batching off, multiplex=on for small, batching windows 10ms/25ms as noted. KV cache hit rates swept at 90%, 70%, 40%.
- Metric capture: p50/p90/p99 generation latency (ms), tokens/sec, dollars per 1k queries (simple infra cost model + model cost proxies).

Representative numeric sketches (rounded)
- Per-1k query cost estimate (incl infra fraction):
  * Small (7B q4): $0.32/1k (micro), $0.35/1k (burst), $0.36/1k (sustained)
  * Medium (13B q4): $0.88/1k (micro), $0.92/1k (burst), $0.90/1k (sustained)
  * Large (70B q8): $3.20/1k (micro), $3.40/1k (burst), $3.35/1k (sustained)

- Latency p50 / p90 (ms), burst scenario, KV hit 70%:
  Model | p50 | p90 | p99
  small  |  65 | 210 | 380
  medium | 110 | 395 | 820
  large  | 230 | 830 | 1650

ASCII micro-visual: p90 vs $/1k (burst, KV=70%)
  $/1k  ^
  3.5  |                         LARG E( p90=830ms )
  2.5  |                MEDIUM( p90=395ms )
  1.0  |    SMALL ( p90=210ms )
  0.0  +----------------------------------> p90(ms)
        0   200   400   600   800   1000

Observations and fodder for product decisions:
1) Micro-session economics: small tier wins decisively on $/1k for single-turn interactions. If product SLA is p90 < 300ms, small tier + light prefetch meets it at <0.4$/1k.
2) Bursty tail sensitivity: under burst with KV hit dropping to 40%, p90 for medium jumps ~1.8x and cost per 1k increases slightly due to extra fallback to large (or queue dwell). That suggests we need soft-fallback routing thresholds tied to KV diagnostics.
3) Handshake window (a configurable client-side prefetched handshake that primes KV) reduces observed p90 more for medium than small — i.e., medium benefits more from prefetching because its kernel selection suffers more at cold start. A 300–400ms handshake window was the knee for medium.
4) Quantization trade: q4 reduces $/1k 20-30% vs q8 on large but adds decode jitter for long context (p99 risk). Hybrid serving paths (start q4, escalate to q8 at token N or on quality triggers) look promising.

Run notes (most runs are noisy - keep as decisions, not final data):
- Batch window increased to 25ms improved throughput but added ~10–15ms p50 in micro-session. Not worth it for small session-first products.
- Multiplexing small clients onto a shared fast-path reduced cost by ~8% and left p90 flat; promising for PLG tier.
- We saw a pathological case with fingerprinted sessions that forced cache churn (p90 spike ~2.1x) — requires better session affinity heuristics for medium->large steering.

Suggested experiments (next week sprint):
- Sweep handshake window (0ms, 100ms, 300ms, 600ms) for medium tier across KV hit levels to quantify where marginal p90 improvements stop. Owner: Evan.
- Implement simple escalate-after-N-tokens for quant profile (q4->q8 at 256 tokens) and run long-context decode trials. Owner: María.
- Small-tier multiplex policy: simulate 5x PLG concurrency with opportunistic prefetch to measure client impact at p90 and cost. Owner: Luca.

Quick decision table (tradeoffs):
- Use small-tier as default for single-turn microfeatures (chat snippets, short completions). Pros: lowest $/1k, low p50. Cons: fragile under large-session churn.
- Medium-tier with 300–400ms handshake as a mid-SLA path for general-purpose chat. Pros: good latency/cost balance. Cons: needs affinity + prefetch tuning.
- Large-tier reserved for long-context, high-quality decode where p99 and quality matter.

Open questions / things we didn't get to:
- How does the same tiering behave with edge-region placement (added network jitter)? Quick thought: p90 grows additively; handshake becomes more valuable.
- Need real $/1k mapping to billing model (tokenized pricing vs infra amortization) before customer collateral.
- Should Console show default handshake knobs in the template for medium-tier routes? Probably yes, but need guardrails.

Unresolved notes (TODOs in doc):
- Add a small CSV of raw run outputs (Evan has raw logs, link above).
- Coordinate with Metrics to ensure we have a p99 labeling tag for session-affinity churn.
- Draft a short one-pager for Solutions describing recommended defaults for PLG vs paid tenants.

Rough TL;DR line for comms (one sentence):
"Tiering + modest prefetching delivers best $/1k for short interactions while preserving acceptable p50; medium-tier handshake defaults reduce burst tail risk but require session affinity and quantization escalation for long-context workloads."

Notes-to-self style:
- This is a sketchy-run capture — don't present externally yet.
- Keep this in product-optimize backlog as 'vel-tiering' cluster.
- If we get a channel ask for rough numbers, use the per-1k figures above but call them 'internal sketch estimates' and attach raw run ids.

End of notes.
